title: Chronological scratch compaction and ephemeral KV binning
author: Priya Natarajan
description: Background: Production workloads with mixed sequence lengths were showing elevated transient GPU memory usage due to long-lived scratch allocations and conservative KV retention. Motivation: Reduce peak working set without regressing latency SLOs by compacting scratch buffers along a chronological lifetime axis and introducing an ephemeral KV binning layer to enable low-overhead short-term eviction. Design summary: 1) Chronological scratch compaction: a micro-slab allocator subdivides large scratch arenas into thin chronological slabs keyed to request arrival time windows. Slabs are compacted (coalesced and zeroed) once all active kernels referencing that slab have completed; we prioritized an optimistic fast-path for single-kernel consumers and a fallback slow-path that defers compaction for multi-kernel overlap. 2) Ephemeral KV binning: add a short-lived in-GPU bin layer for KV cache entries produced by streaming/continuous-batching traffic. Bins are sized by recent token reuse statistics and are evicted in short time windows (seconds) before falling back to the regular LRU eviction policy. 3) Kernel handshake and scheduler hints: small ABI extension lets kernels declare scratch slab affinity and earliest-safe-evict timestamps to avoid races during aggressive compaction. 4) Safety/fallbacks: compaction is gated behind runtime flags and a conservative heuristics mode that disables binning for pinned sessions (dedicated capacity). Checklist: - [x] implementation of micro-slab allocator and slab lifecycle manager - [x] ephemeral KV binning + telemetry - [x] scheduler handshake + kernel ABI extension - [x] unit & integration tests - [x] microbench/perf runs and SLO verification - [x] rollout plan with runtime flag & canary gating Testing & results: Unit tests added for allocator invariants and KV bin rotation. Integration tests simulate mixed-length streaming workloads and show median peak GPU working set reduced by ~18% on T4/GPU mix and up to 27% on p4d tests with heavy continuous-batching. P99 latency change: +1.3% (within allowable SLO); throughput unchanged. Safety: feature off by default for hosted API; enabled behind canary boolean for Dedicated. Rollout: staged canary (10% nodes) for 48h then ramp to 100% if no regressions. Related: touches runtime/scheduler, runtime/scratch_allocator, runtime/kv_cache, and a small API bump for kernel metadata. Notes: This PR is focused on runtime memory and low-risk integration—there are follow-ups planned to expose additional telemetry and per-customer tuning knobs in Redwood Console.
